chunks: And in the narration of Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Thaqafī, he said:

Two men entrusted a woman with a deposit and said to her, 'Do not hand it over to either one of us until we both come together before you.' Then they departed and were absent. One of them came to her and said, 'Give me my deposit, for my companion has died.' She refused until his repeated coming to her increased, then she gave it to him.

Then the other one came and said, 'Bring me my deposit.' She said, 'Your companion took it and mentioned that you had died.' Then they took the dispute to ʿUmar, and ʿUmar said to her, 'I do not see except that you have become liable.'
So the woman said, 'Appoint ʿAlī عليه السلام between me and him.' So he said to him, 'Judge between them.'

Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said, 'This deposit is with her, and you both instructed her not to hand it over to either one of you until you both came together before her. So bring me your companion.' And he did not hold her liable.
And ʿAlī عليه السلام said, 'They only intended to take away the woman’s wealth.'

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman involved in the case
key_terms.بِمَالِ: with the property or wealth of
key_terms.وَدِيعَةً: a deposit or entrusted property held in trust

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام judge a case involving a disputed deposit and alleged liability?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a legal dispute over a deposited trust and shows the judicial insight of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in uncovering attempted fraud. It highlights principles of trust, liability, and careful adjudication, showing that the woman was not automatically responsible when she had originally been bound by the depositors’ joint condition.
